paragraphs.title: The Land’s Sabbath and the Lord’s Command

easy.question: Who spoke to Moses?
answers: The Lord
Pharaoh
Joshua
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord spoke to Moses.”

easy.question: Where did the Lord speak to Moses?
answers: In Egypt
At Mount Sinai
In Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The verse says that He spoke to Moses at Mount Sinai.

easy.question: To whom was Moses told to speak?
answers: Pharaoh
The priests only
The children of Israel
easy.explanation: Moses was told, “Speak to the children of Israel.”

medium.question: What order of events is described in the verses?
answers: The Lord speaks to Moses, and Moses is told to speak to Israel
Israel speaks to Moses, and then the Lord speaks to them
Moses enters the land, and then the Lord speaks to him
medium.explanation: First the Lord speaks to Moses, and then commands him to speak to Israel.

medium.question: What will happen when Israel comes into the land the Lord gives them?
answers: They will leave the land
The land will keep a sabbath to the Lord
They will build Mount Sinai
medium.explanation: The verse says, “The land shall keep a sabbath unto the Lord.”

medium.question: What does “keep a sabbath” mean here?
answers: Disappear
Be covered with water
Rest from agricultural work
medium.explanation: The land is to rest and cease from ordinary farming.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “the land which I give you”?
answers: The land is presented as a gift from the Lord
Israel bought the land
The land belongs only to Moses
challenge.explanation: The Lord describes the land as land that He gives to Israel.

challenge.question: What does “unto the Lord” emphasize?
answers: The land rests only at night
The rest has religious meaning and is dedicated to the Lord
The land will pass to another nation
challenge.explanation: The land’s rest is an act connected with worship of the Lord.

challenge.question: What detail may seem surprising?
answers: The command came only after Israel lived there for many years
Moses spoke to Pharaoh at Mount Sinai
The command was given at Sinai even though it concerns a land Israel would enter in the future
challenge.explanation: The command is given at Sinai, while the verse speaks of Israel’s future arrival in the land.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “the land which I give you”?
answers: The land is presented as a gift from the Lord
Israel bought the land
The land belongs only to Moses
questions.explanation: The Lord describes the land as land that He gives to Israel.

questions.question: What does “unto the Lord” emphasize?
answers: The land rests only at night
The rest has religious meaning and is dedicated to the Lord
The land will pass to another nation
questions.explanation: The land’s rest is an act connected with worship of the Lord.

questions.question: What detail may seem surprising?
answers: The command came only after Israel lived there for many years
Moses spoke to Pharaoh at Mount Sinai
The command was given at Sinai even though it concerns a land Israel would enter in the future
questions.explanation: The command is given at Sinai, while the verse speaks of Israel’s future arrival in the land.

paragraphs.title: Six Years of Work and the Sabbatical Year

easy.question: For how many years must a person sow his field?
answers: Six years
Seven years
One year
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Six years thou shalt sow thy field.”

easy.question: What must be done in the seventh year?
answers: Sow more seed
Give the land a complete rest
Gather the entire harvest
easy.explanation: The seventh year is a year of rest for the land.

easy.question: Who may eat the produce during the year of rest?
answers: Only the landowner
Only the priests
People, servants, livestock, and wild animals
easy.explanation: The verses list people, servants, hired workers, strangers, livestock, and animals.

medium.question: What sequence of years is described?
answers: Six years of work followed by one year of rest
One year of rest followed by six years of work
Seven consecutive years of work
medium.explanation: The field and vineyard are worked for six years, and the seventh year is a rest.

medium.question: What does “what groweth of its own accord” refer to?
answers: A harvesting tool
Plants that grow again without being planted
An unusually large grape
medium.explanation: It refers to growth that comes up by itself after the harvest.

medium.question: What is one result of the prohibition against working in the seventh year?
answers: Only the owner may eat the produce
No one may eat the produce
The produce is available for people and animals
medium.explanation: The sabbath produce is described as food for people and animals.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from mentioning the animals of the land?
answers: The produce is not intended only for human beings
Animals must work in the fields
Animals may not eat from the land
challenge.explanation: The produce is available to animals as well as people.

challenge.question: Why is the seventh year called a “sabbath of rest”?
answers: Only a little work is done
It is a complete rest for the land
It is reserved only for celebrations
challenge.explanation: The term emphasizes that sowing, pruning, reaping, and gathering are prohibited.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the food is not limited to the owner’s family?
answers: The vineyard is mentioned
Six years of work are mentioned
Servants, hired workers, and strangers are listed
challenge.explanation: The list includes those who live and work with the owner, not just his family.

questions.question: What can be inferred from mentioning the animals of the land?
answers: The produce is not intended only for human beings
Animals must work in the fields
Animals may not eat from the land
questions.explanation: The produce is available to animals as well as people.

questions.question: Why is the seventh year called a “sabbath of rest”?
answers: Only a little work is done
It is a complete rest for the land
It is reserved only for celebrations
questions.explanation: The term emphasizes that sowing, pruning, reaping, and gathering are prohibited.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the food is not limited to the owner’s family?
answers: The vineyard is mentioned
Six years of work are mentioned
Servants, hired workers, and strangers are listed
questions.explanation: The list includes those who live and work with the owner, not just his family.

paragraphs.title: Counting the Years and the Jubilee

easy.question: How many years are counted before the Jubilee year?
answers: Forty-nine years
Forty years
Seventy years
easy.explanation: Seven periods of seven years total forty-nine years.

easy.question: On what day is the Jubilee trumpet sounded?
answers: The first day of the year
The Day of Atonement
The Feast of Tabernacles
easy.explanation: The trumpet is sounded on the tenth day of the seventh month, the Day of Atonement.

easy.question: What happens in the Jubilee year?
answers: Everyone goes to war
The festivals stop
Each person returns to his possession and family
easy.explanation: The verse says that everyone returns to his possession and family.

medium.question: How is the Jubilee year reached?
answers: Seven times seven years are counted, followed by the fiftieth year
Five times ten years are counted, followed by the fortieth year
Ten times five years are counted, followed by the sixtieth year
medium.explanation: Seven sabbaths of years equal forty-nine years, followed by the fiftieth year.

medium.question: What does “liberty” mean in the Jubilee proclamation?
answers: Harvest
Freedom and release
A trumpet blast
medium.explanation: The proclamation announces freedom throughout the land.

medium.question: Why are sowing and reaping prohibited in the Jubilee year?
answers: It is holy and set apart for rest
There are no fields in the land
Only imported fruit may be eaten
medium.explanation: Because the year is holy, ordinary agricultural work is not done.

challenge.question: Which description accurately matches the Jubilee proclamation?
answers: A trumpet is sounded on the Day of Atonement, in the seventh month and on the tenth day, throughout the land
A trumpet is sounded on the first day of the year in Jerusalem only
A trumpet is sounded at the Feast of Tabernacles in each city separately
challenge.explanation: The verse specifies the seventh month, the tenth day, the Day of Atonement, and the whole land.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from everyone returning to his possession?
answers: People could not move between cities
Land transfers were not meant to be permanent
All possessions became equal in size
challenge.explanation: The return shows that land rights were restored rather than transferred forever.

challenge.question: How could Israel eat during the Jubilee if sowing and reaping were prohibited?
answers: They received food from other countries
They ate only bread saved from earlier years
They ate the produce that grew in the field without ordinary cultivation
challenge.explanation: The verse says they would eat the field’s produce without normal sowing and reaping.

questions.question: Which description accurately matches the Jubilee proclamation?
answers: A trumpet is sounded on the Day of Atonement, in the seventh month and on the tenth day, throughout the land
A trumpet is sounded on the first day of the year in Jerusalem only
A trumpet is sounded at the Feast of Tabernacles in each city separately
questions.explanation: The verse specifies the seventh month, the tenth day, the Day of Atonement, and the whole land.

questions.question: What can be inferred from everyone returning to his possession?
answers: People could not move between cities
Land transfers were not meant to be permanent
All possessions became equal in size
questions.explanation: The return shows that land rights were restored rather than transferred forever.

questions.question: How could Israel eat during the Jubilee if sowing and reaping were prohibited?
answers: They received food from other countries
They ate only bread saved from earlier years
They ate the produce that grew in the field without ordinary cultivation
questions.explanation: The verse says they would eat the field’s produce without normal sowing and reaping.

paragraphs.title: Fair Trade According to the Years of Produce

easy.question: What must not be done when buying from or selling to a neighbor?
answers: Oppress or cheat him
Bless him
Help him
easy.explanation: The verses prohibit oppressing one another in a transaction.

easy.question: What determines the sale price?
answers: The size of the house
The number of years and harvests
The number of children
easy.explanation: The price is based on the years and the number of harvests until Jubilee.

easy.question: Whom must a person fear?
answers: His neighbor
The king
His God
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt fear thy God.”

medium.question: What happens to the price when many years remain until Jubilee?
answers: It always decreases
It increases
It is unrelated to the number of years
medium.explanation: More remaining years mean more harvests and therefore a higher price.

medium.question: What does “oppress” mean in this business context?
answers: Take unfair advantage of or cheat your neighbor
Invite your neighbor as a guest
Lend money to your neighbor
medium.explanation: The command prohibits taking unfair advantage of someone in a transaction.

medium.question: Why is the price connected to the number of harvests?
answers: The harvest is unrelated to the sale
Only the rich may buy
What is really being sold is the number of harvests remaining until Jubilee
medium.explanation: The passage explains that the number of harvests determines the value.

challenge.question: Why should the price be lower when Jubilee is near?
answers: Selling before Jubilee is forbidden
Fewer years of harvest remain to be enjoyed
The produce becomes more expensive
challenge.explanation: When Jubilee is near, fewer years and harvests remain, so the sale is worth less.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the prohibition applies to both sides of the transaction?
answers: Only the buyer is mentioned
Only the seller is mentioned
Both buyer and seller are told not to oppress one another
challenge.explanation: The command addresses both parties and then prohibits oppressing one another.

challenge.question: What central idea explains why cheating is forbidden?
answers: The price depends on time and harvests, so it must be calculated honestly
Every transaction must be free
Trade itself is forbidden
challenge.explanation: Because the price depends on years and harvests, the parties must deal honestly.

questions.question: Why should the price be lower when Jubilee is near?
answers: Selling before Jubilee is forbidden
Fewer years of harvest remain to be enjoyed
The produce becomes more expensive
questions.explanation: When Jubilee is near, fewer years and harvests remain, so the sale is worth less.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the prohibition applies to both sides of the transaction?
answers: Only the buyer is mentioned
Only the seller is mentioned
Both buyer and seller are told not to oppress one another
questions.explanation: The command addresses both parties and then prohibits oppressing one another.

questions.question: What central idea explains why cheating is forbidden?
answers: The price depends on time and harvests, so it must be calculated honestly
Every transaction must be free
Trade itself is forbidden
questions.explanation: Because the price depends on years and harvests, the parties must deal honestly.

paragraphs.title: Keeping the Laws and the Land’s Blessing

easy.question: What will happen if Israel keeps the Lord’s statutes and judgments?
answers: They will dwell safely in the land
They will leave the land
They will not eat the land’s produce
easy.explanation: The verse promises that they will dwell in the land safely.

easy.question: What will the land provide?
answers: Water only
Its fruit, enough to satisfy you
New houses
easy.explanation: The land will yield its fruit, and the people will eat their fill.

easy.question: What will they not do in the seventh year?
answers: Eat at all
Live in the land
Sow or gather the harvest
easy.explanation: They will not sow or gather in the seventh year.

medium.question: What will the Lord do in the sixth year?
answers: Bless the produce so it will last for three years
Command them to sow in the seventh year
Stop the crops from growing
medium.explanation: The Lord promises a sixth-year harvest sufficient for three years.

medium.question: What is the sequence described?
answers: Harvest in the seventh year, sow in the eighth, and eat in the ninth
Receive blessing in the sixth, sow in the eighth, and eat old produce until the new harvest arrives
Sow in the sixth, gather in the seventh, and stop eating in the eighth
medium.explanation: The sixth year brings blessing; after the seventh-year rest, sowing resumes in the eighth.

medium.question: What does “eat your fill” mean?
answers: Eat secretly
Eat quickly
Have enough food until satisfied
medium.explanation: The phrase means to eat enough so that one is no longer hungry.

challenge.question: Why are the Israelites concerned about the seventh year, and what solution is promised?
answers: They fear a lack of food, and the sixth-year harvest will provide for them
They fear war, and the solution is leaving the land
They fear a lack of water, and the solution is sowing in the seventh year
challenge.explanation: Because they will not sow or gather in the seventh year, the Lord promises a sufficient sixth-year harvest.

challenge.question: What is implied by “until the ninth year’s produce comes in”?
answers: Only new fruit is eaten in the eighth year
Old produce is eaten until the new produce arrives
The old produce is discarded at the start of the eighth year
challenge.explanation: The old harvest remains available until the new harvest arrives.

challenge.question: What condition-and-result relationship appears here?
answers: If they do not sow in the seventh year, the land will never produce again
If they sow in the eighth year, they need no sixth-year produce
Keeping the Lord’s laws is connected with dwelling safely and receiving abundant crops
challenge.explanation: The passage links obedience with security and a blessed harvest.

questions.question: Why are the Israelites concerned about the seventh year, and what solution is promised?
answers: They fear a lack of food, and the sixth-year harvest will provide for them
They fear war, and the solution is leaving the land
They fear a lack of water, and the solution is sowing in the seventh year
questions.explanation: Because they will not sow or gather in the seventh year, the Lord promises a sufficient sixth-year harvest.

questions.question: What is implied by “until the ninth year’s produce comes in”?
answers: Only new fruit is eaten in the eighth year
Old produce is eaten until the new produce arrives
The old produce is discarded at the start of the eighth year
questions.explanation: The old harvest remains available until the new harvest arrives.

questions.question: What condition-and-result relationship appears here?
answers: If they do not sow in the seventh year, the land will never produce again
If they sow in the eighth year, they need no sixth-year produce
Keeping the Lord’s laws is connected with dwelling safely and receiving abundant crops
questions.explanation: The passage links obedience with security and a blessed harvest.

paragraphs.title: The Land Belongs to the Lord

easy.question: What must not be done to the land?
answers: Sold permanently
Cultivated
Watered
easy.explanation: The verse says that the land must not be sold forever.

easy.question: To whom does the land belong?
answers: The king
God
Each family separately
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “The land is mine.”

easy.question: How are the people described in relation to the land?
answers: As absolute owners
As temporary conquerors
As strangers and sojourners with God
easy.explanation: The verse calls them strangers and sojourners with the Lord.

medium.question: What must be granted in every landholding?
answers: A right of redemption
A special tax
A wall around it
medium.explanation: The people are commanded to grant a redemption for the land.

medium.question: What does “forever” mean in “the land shall not be sold for ever”?
answers: Secretly
For a short time
Permanently and without return
medium.explanation: The phrase prohibits an irrevocable, permanent sale.

medium.question: Why may the land not be sold permanently?
answers: It belongs to God, and the people are strangers and sojourners with Him
There is no commerce in the land
People may not work the soil
medium.explanation: The verse gives God’s ownership as the reason.

challenge.question: What follows from prohibiting permanent sale and requiring redemption?
answers: Land may be sold without conditions
A sale can be temporary, with a way to reclaim the land
The land may not be used at all
challenge.explanation: The sale is not final because redemption remains possible.

challenge.question: What does “with me” teach about people’s status?
answers: People alone own the land
People may not live in the land
People live in the land under God’s ownership
challenge.explanation: They live there as sojourners alongside God, not as absolute owners.

challenge.question: What does “in all the land of your possession” emphasize?
answers: The rule applies throughout the land they possess
The rule applies only to the capital
The rule applies only to priestly land
challenge.explanation: The command applies to every part of their landholding.

questions.question: What follows from prohibiting permanent sale and requiring redemption?
answers: Land may be sold without conditions
A sale can be temporary, with a way to reclaim the land
The land may not be used at all
questions.explanation: The sale is not final because redemption remains possible.

questions.question: What does “with me” teach about people’s status?
answers: People alone own the land
People may not live in the land
People live in the land under God’s ownership
questions.explanation: They live there as sojourners alongside God, not as absolute owners.

questions.question: What does “in all the land of your possession” emphasize?
answers: The rule applies throughout the land they possess
The rule applies only to the capital
The rule applies only to priestly land
questions.explanation: The command applies to every part of their landholding.

easy.question: Who may redeem a brother’s possession?
answers: A close relative
Only the buyer
Any stranger
easy.explanation: A close relative may redeem what his brother sold.

easy.question: What did the brother sell when he became poor?
answers: Only his house
His possession
The buyer’s property
easy.explanation: The verse speaks of selling part of his possession.

easy.question: What happens if the possession cannot be redeemed before Jubilee?
answers: It remains with the buyer forever
It passes to the king
It returns to its owner at Jubilee
easy.explanation: At Jubilee the sold possession goes out and returns to its owner.

medium.question: What must a person do if he obtains enough money to redeem his possession?
answers: Calculate the years, repay the proper amount, and regain the possession
Pay a fixed price without counting the years
Wait for someone else to redeem it
medium.explanation: He calculates the value according to the remaining years and restores the proper amount.

medium.question: What does “the price of his redemption” refer to?
answers: His nearest relative
The amount required to redeem the possession
The Jubilee year
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the money needed for redemption.

medium.question: Why may a relative redeem the possession?
answers: So the buyer will profit more
To cancel the Jubilee
To keep the land within the family
medium.explanation: Redemption allows the family to recover the possession.

challenge.question: What is the difference between someone able to redeem his possession and someone unable to do so?
answers: The first can redeem it immediately; the second waits until Jubilee
The first loses it; the second receives another possession
There is no difference
challenge.explanation: A person with sufficient means can redeem it, while the other waits for Jubilee.

challenge.question: What does calculating the years and repaying the surplus show?
answers: The price is unrelated to time
The price depends on the years remaining until Jubilee
The buyer must always receive all the money again
challenge.explanation: The payment is adjusted according to how long the buyer held the possession.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the sale is not permanent?
answers: The buyer may immediately resell it
A relative must redeem it in every case
The possession returns at Jubilee even if it was not previously redeemed
challenge.explanation: Jubilee ends the sale and restores the possession.

questions.question: What is the difference between someone able to redeem his possession and someone unable to do so?
answers: The first can redeem it immediately; the second waits until Jubilee
The first loses it; the second receives another possession
There is no difference
questions.explanation: A person with sufficient means can redeem it, while the other waits for Jubilee.

questions.question: What does calculating the years and repaying the surplus show?
answers: The price is unrelated to time
The price depends on the years remaining until Jubilee
The buyer must always receive all the money again
questions.explanation: The payment is adjusted according to how long the buyer held the possession.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the sale is not permanent?
answers: The buyer may immediately resell it
A relative must redeem it in every case
The possession returns at Jubilee even if it was not previously redeemed
questions.explanation: Jubilee ends the sale and restores the possession.

paragraphs.title: Selling a House in a Walled City

easy.question: What is sold in these verses?
answers: A house in a walled city
An open field
An animal
easy.explanation: The passage concerns a dwelling house in a walled city.

easy.question: How long may the house be redeemed?
answers: Ten years
One full year after the sale
Only at Jubilee
easy.explanation: The house may be redeemed during the full year after it is sold.

easy.question: What happens if it is not redeemed within the year?
answers: It immediately returns to the seller
It is destroyed
It remains permanently with the buyer
easy.explanation: After the year ends, the house belongs permanently to the buyer and his descendants.

medium.question: Why does it matter that the house is in a walled city?
answers: A special rule applies to such a house
Houses in walled cities may not be sold
The house must be outside the city
medium.explanation: The verses establish a special rule for a house in a walled city.

medium.question: What does “established for ever” mean here?
answers: For a short time
Permanently, without returning to the seller
Only until the end of that year
medium.explanation: The house remains with the buyer and his descendants permanently.

medium.question: What is the sequence of events?
answers: The house is sold, there is one year for redemption, and then it remains with the buyer if not redeemed
The house is redeemed and then sold again
The house is sold only after Jubilee
medium.explanation: The passage describes sale, a one-year redemption period, and permanent ownership if it is not redeemed.

challenge.question: What distinguishes this house from possessions that return at Jubilee?
answers: It is in a walled city
It belongs to a priest
It is sold only to a poor person
challenge.explanation: A house in a walled city does not go out at Jubilee if it was not redeemed during the first year.

challenge.question: What is meant by “it shall not go out in the jubile”?
answers: The house must be sold at Jubilee
The house does not return to the seller at Jubilee
The house is destroyed at Jubilee
challenge.explanation: Jubilee does not cancel the buyer’s ownership of this house.

challenge.question: What is the purpose of limiting redemption to one year?
answers: To give the seller a limited time to recover the house
To prevent the buyer from using it for a year
To wait until the house becomes a field
challenge.explanation: The seller has a chance to redeem it, but only during the first year.

questions.question: What distinguishes this house from possessions that return at Jubilee?
answers: It is in a walled city
It belongs to a priest
It is sold only to a poor person
questions.explanation: A house in a walled city does not go out at Jubilee if it was not redeemed during the first year.

questions.question: What is meant by “it shall not go out in the jubile”?
answers: The house must be sold at Jubilee
The house does not return to the seller at Jubilee
The house is destroyed at Jubilee
questions.explanation: Jubilee does not cancel the buyer’s ownership of this house.

questions.question: What is the purpose of limiting redemption to one year?
answers: To give the seller a limited time to recover the house
To prevent the buyer from using it for a year
To wait until the house becomes a field
questions.explanation: The seller has a chance to redeem it, but only during the first year.

easy.question: What happens to a house in an unwalled village at Jubilee?
answers: It goes out to its owner
It is destroyed
It is sold to the Levites
easy.explanation: Such houses are counted as fields and return at Jubilee.

easy.question: Who may redeem houses in the cities of their possession at any time?
answers: All Israelites
The Levites
The king
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Levites may redeem them at any time.

easy.question: What is said about the field of the suburbs of the Levite cities?
answers: It may be sold only at Jubilee
It is given to Israel
It may not be sold
easy.explanation: The field is the Levites’ perpetual possession and may not be sold.

medium.question: Why may the Levites redeem their houses at any time?
answers: Their houses were outside Israel
Their cities were their possession among Israel
They received no cities
medium.explanation: The Levitical cities were their permanent possession among the Israelites.

medium.question: What is a “suburb” in this context?
answers: Open land adjoining the city
The wall around the city
A market inside the city
medium.explanation: It refers to the open land surrounding the city.

medium.question: What is the main difference between an unwalled house and a Levitical house?
answers: An unwalled house cannot be redeemed
A Levitical house is sold permanently
An unwalled house returns at Jubilee, while a Levitical house may always be redeemed
medium.explanation: Unwalled houses have the rule of fields; Levitical houses have perpetual redemption.

challenge.question: What follows from unwalled houses being counted as fields?
answers: They have the rule of fields rather than the rule of walled-city houses
No one may live in them
They always belong to the Levites
challenge.explanation: Because they are treated as fields, they return at Jubilee.

challenge.question: What does “among the children of Israel” show about the Levites’ cities?
answers: The Levites lived outside the camp
Their cities were distributed among Israel’s tribal lands
All Israelites lived in Levite cities
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that Levite cities were located among the other tribes.

challenge.question: What special rule applies to the suburban field?
answers: It returns after one hundred years
It may be sold only to Levites
It may not be sold because it is a perpetual possession
challenge.explanation: Unlike a house, the suburban field is protected from sale.

questions.question: What follows from unwalled houses being counted as fields?
answers: They have the rule of fields rather than the rule of walled-city houses
No one may live in them
They always belong to the Levites
questions.explanation: Because they are treated as fields, they return at Jubilee.

questions.question: What does “among the children of Israel” show about the Levites’ cities?
answers: The Levites lived outside the camp
Their cities were distributed among Israel’s tribal lands
All Israelites lived in Levite cities
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that Levite cities were located among the other tribes.

questions.question: What special rule applies to the suburban field?
answers: It returns after one hundred years
It may be sold only to Levites
It may not be sold because it is a perpetual possession
questions.explanation: Unlike a house, the suburban field is protected from sale.

easy.question: What should be done when a brother becomes poor?
answers: Strengthen and help him
Avoid him
Take more money from him
easy.explanation: The command is to relieve and support him.

easy.question: What must not be taken from the poor brother?
answers: Help
Usury or increase
Food and water
easy.explanation: The passage prohibits charging usury or interest.

easy.question: Who brought Israel out of Egypt?
answers: Moses
The king of Canaan
The Lord
easy.explanation: The Lord says that He brought Israel out of Egypt.

medium.question: What is the connection between the brother’s poverty and “that thy brother may live with thee”?
answers: Leave him to himself
Help him so that he can survive
Charge him a tax
medium.explanation: The poor person is to be supported so that he can live within the community.

medium.question: What does “usury” mean here?
answers: An animal’s bite
A large gift
Interest charged on a loan
medium.explanation: The context concerns money and food lent to a brother, so usury means added interest.

medium.question: Why does the passage say, “fear thy God,” after forbidding interest?
answers: To remind people that God forbids exploiting the poor
To teach people to fear the poor
To permit a small amount of interest
medium.explanation: Fear of God reinforces the duty not to exploit a needy brother.

A foreigner or resident living among the people
Only a priest’s family

answers: “That thy brother may live with thee”
“Out of the land of Egypt”
“Nor lend him thy victuals for increase”

The Exodus removes the duty to help the poor
Canaan was given only to people who charge interest
challenge.explanation: God’s redemption and gift of the land establish a community marked by justice and care.

Give him an inheritance

Until he finds another job
Until the Jubilee year

To Egypt
To the buyer’s house

He is sold because of poverty, serves as a hired servant until Jubilee, and returns home

answers: With harsh and cruel labor
With brief work
With voluntary work

He serves as a hired servant and is not ruled over as a slave
He may sell the buyer

Everyone in the city

Only from Israelites
Only from priests

A place of prayer

Israelites may be ruled over harshly

answers: Any stranger
One of his brothers
Only the foreigner
easy.explanation: The verse says that one of his brothers may redeem him.

answers: The foreigner’s agreement

His ability to pay

Redemption is forbidden
He becomes a foreigner

He becomes poor
He is punished

Punished
Released or bought back

Only the oldest brother must redeem him
Only the man himself may be redeemed

The foreigner must release him immediately

Redemption remains possible after the sale

The Lord
